rounds.text: Avalon Technologies Ltd is demonstrating stellar top-line and bottom-line momentum, underpinned by a compounded profit growth of 40% over 5 years and a striking 70% growth in trailing twelve months profit [E17, E19]. This rapid expansion is matched by accelerating operational efficiency, evidenced by an operating margin climbing to 12% in the TTM from 7% three years earlier and reaching 13% in September 2026 [E25, E26]. The market is taking notice of this superior fundamental delivery, with the rules-based screen awarding the company a high-confidence BUY score of 84 out of 100 [E61]. Furthermore, institutional sponsorship is robustly expanding; foreign institutions increased their holding to 11.13% and domestic institutions to 21.82% since December 2023, driving a positive institutional money flow signal [E37, E38, E39]. This institutional accumulation is supported by a solid relative-strength rating of 77 against the Nifty 500 alongside a healthy 1.05 Sharpe ratio [E46, E50]. Conceded: the stock trades at a demanding P/E of 77.9x and price-to-book of 14.52x, with a reverse DCF implying an aggressive 27.1% earnings growth expectation [E1, E2, E42].

Avalon Technologies carries an extreme valuation that is completely detached from fundamental reality, trading at a P/E of 77.9x against a sector benchmark of just 21.76x, and a price-to-book ratio of 14.52x compared to a sector average of 2.32x [E1, E6, E7]. This excessive pricing leaves virtually zero margin of safety, with a discounted cash flow model pegging intrinsic value at Rs 901 against the current market price of Rs 1,728, representing a severe overvaluation of -91.7% [E40, E41]. Furthermore, a reverse DCF reveals that the market price already prices in an aggressive 27.1% earnings growth rate, surpassing the base case expectation of 18.0% and signaling that expectations are dangerously running ahead of actual delivery [E42, E52]. Balance sheet and cash flow metrics reinforce these underlying concerns, evidenced by a cash conversion ratio of just 0.50x where profits significantly outpace actual operating cash flow, alongside a sharp rise in borrowings to Rs 341 Cr in September 2026 from Rs 213 Cr a year prior [E29, E34]. Compounding the risk profile, promoters have been steadily reducing their stake, dropping from 50.98% in December 2023 to 40.35% by September 2026 [E36], and the stock exhibits high annualised volatility of 52.3% [E49].
